correctness.rationale: For every irreducible finite doubly stochastic P the restriction A=I-P^T to the zero-sum hyperplane is invertible. Rank-one stationarity implies the exact finite response law u_epsilon=u0+epsilon A^-1(e_k-e_j)/[n(1-epsilon(A^-1d)_i)]; incidence differences span a dimension n-c subspace, and exact finite measurements on a spanning tree recover A^-1 and P. A six-state rational counterexample is doubly stochastic, irreducible and aperiodic but has c=2. Exact rational runnable tests verify the example and reconstruct a chiral four-state model from three finite observations. No finite checker is confused with proof of all n.

value.rationale: Calvert 2026 motivates detection of hidden kinetics despite occupation proportional to inverse exit rate. The graph-only n-c test gives a complete observability boundary under physically constrained individual outgoing reallocation, the spanning-tree design extracts the whole unknown network from finite static experiments, and the aperiodic example shows mixing alone does not make such experiments complete. Narrow scope and sampling limitations are disclosed; no general downstream theorem required.
